Leaderboard
Challenge a friend
HEAD-TO-HEAD PRACTICE
Challenge a friend to a 30-day duel

Send a link, both of you trade the simulator for 30 days, and the scoreboard compares server-recorded percentage change from each participant's own starting value at acceptance. Final scores use the last server-cached quotes available at the deadline. Scores are simulated. No real money is involved.

Duels need a free account so both scores can be tracked. Core simulator and learning features work without signing in; community profiles, ranked scores and duels require an account.

Create a free account
1. Create a link

Create an invitation from a ranked practice portfolio. Browser imports cannot enter duels.

2. Your friend joins

When they accept, both starting values are recorded together and the 30-day clock begins.

3. 30 days of practice

Scores use server-recorded trades and cached valuation quotes. Final values are calculated at the deadline and then frozen.

How duel scoring works

A duel compares percentage change, not dollar totals. If you begin a duel at $104,000 of simulated equity and finish at $109,200, your duel score is +5.0% — the $4,000 you were already up before the duel started does not count. Your friend is measured the same way from their own starting line. Server-scored duels use server-recorded trades and cached quotes. Legacy client-summary duels are labelled separately and do not have reconstructed final scores. These are practice data rather than audited investment results.

Nothing is reset when a duel begins. Your practice portfolio, journal and watchlist stay exactly as they were, and losing a duel has no effect on your account. The purpose is deliberate practice under a deadline, which is the same reason trading educators use timed paper-trading exercises.

(Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

TradeHQ is an educational paper trading simulator. No real money is traded. Nothing on this website constitutes investment, financial, legal or tax advice. Past simulated performance does not predict future real-world performance.

supplementaryNotes.text:
Learning notes: Challenge a Friend

Create a shareable invite for a 30-day practice duel. Each participant is measured from their own recorded starting value, using server-recorded trades and deadline-frozen simulated scores. Educational simulation only.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

How a practice duel works

Create an invite link and send it to a friend. Both starting values are recorded when the invitation is accepted; the values can differ. The page shows a 30-day countdown and compares server-recorded simulated percentage changes. Final scores use trades and the last cached valuation quotes available at the deadline and are then frozen. Older client-summary duels are labelled legacy because reliable final values cannot be recovered.

Nothing is wagered and nothing is won. There is no entry fee, no prize pool and no real money at any point — this is a study device that uses mild competition to make daily practice stick.

Rules that make a duel actually useful
For a virtual challenge, agree on the example's quantity and exposure assumptions; TradeHQ does not provide leverage or real-money wagering.
If participants choose to keep a virtual journal, compare stated assumptions and data-source labels rather than treating ranking as a measure of investment ability.
Compare the illustrated drawdowns and simulated returns without claiming they establish superior real-world skill.
Discuss which hypothetical assumptions were missing or changed; there is no prize or real-money outcome.
What a duel does and does not prove

A 30-day simulated result cannot separate skill from luck or predict who would lead over a year. Concentrated exposure can produce large gains or losses. Compare the stated assumptions and drawdowns without inferring a reliable future ranking.

The useful output of a duel is not the winner but the comparison of two journals covering the same market conditions. Two people who traded the same month and disagreed about what to do will each learn more from the other's reasoning than from the scoreboard.

Practical details
Each participant uses their own recorded starting balance; those balances can differ.
The scoreboard tracks percentage return so different activity levels stay comparable.
The page shows a 30-day countdown based on the recorded duel dates.
There is no fee, no stake, no prize and no real money — running a duel for money would be gambling, and this is not that.
Setting up a duel
Create the duel and copy the invite link that appears.
Send it to one person; the duel starts when they join.
Joining records the second participant's current synced starting value; it does not reset either portfolio.
The scoreboard and countdown appear on this page for both participants for the next 30 days.
The countdown reaching zero does not stop simulator trading. For server-scored duels, final scores are frozen using server-recorded trades and the last cached valuation quotes available at the deadline. Legacy duels have no reconstructed final scores. Neither type is an audited investment record.
